title: 第10章 她亲手布下第一张网
lines: 老太君醒来之后，整个府里表面安静，暗地里却像一根被拉到极限的弦。
清晨，苏晚刚踏出西偏院。
还有她身后的两个嬷嬷。
以及——一群“看热闹”的下人。
苏柔今日换了一身素白衣裙，脸上甚至还刻意带了点憔悴。
看起来像受了天大委屈。
她一见苏晚，就红了眼眶。
苏柔被她这一眼看得心里莫名一紧，但很快又压下去。
苏柔抬起手，轻轻擦了擦眼角。
“昨夜，你房中丢失的那包药粉，是我帮你收着的。”
苏柔继续，声音更低更委屈。
“姐姐你说你要研究医理，我怕你被人发现，就替你收了。”
“可今日……居然在老太君的药里查出来了。”
这一句，像刀子一样落下。
连嬷嬷都下意识后退了一步。
content_zh:
相府的夜，越来越像一张网。

    每一盏灯，都像眼睛。

    每一个脚步声，都像试探。

    而网的中心，是苏晚。

    但没人知道，她已经不再“被困”。

    西偏院。

    夜深。

    风从破窗灌进来，带着寒意。

    苏晚坐在灯下。

    桌上摆着三样东西：

    一碗清水。

    一根银针。

    一张写满字的纸。

    纸上不是医书。

    是相府的“人名”。

    每一个名字后面，都标着两个字——

    “动机”。

    她看得很慢。

    像在复盘一盘棋。

    不是已经下完的棋。

    而是正在改写的棋。

    门外传来脚步声。

    很轻。

    但苏晚已经知道是谁。

    “进来。”

    门开。

    镇北王。

    他一身黑衣，气息冷硬。

    站在门口，没有进来。

    “相府乱了。”

    他说。

    苏晚没有抬头。

    “我知道。”

    镇北王看着她。

    “你做的？”

    苏晚终于笑了一下。

    “不全是。”

    她抬眼。

    “他们自己也很努力。”

    镇北王沉默了一瞬。

    “春杏的局，是你引导的？”

    苏晚点头。

    “我只是没阻止。”

    镇北王皱眉。

    “你在逼他们自乱？”

    苏晚轻声：

    “不是逼。”

    “是让他们选择最蠢的那一步。”

    镇北王盯着她。

    忽然觉得眼前这个人，有点陌生。

    不是“苏晚变了”。

    是——她从一开始就不是他以为的那种人。

    他低声问：

    “你到底想要什么？”

    苏晚停了一下。

    然后说：

    “答案。”
content_en:
The Prime Minister's Mansion was in chaos for the first time.

    It's not superficial chaos.

    It's the kind of chaos where people's hearts begin to crack.

    Chun Xing's body was still parked in the side yard.

    No one dares to come close.

    I dare not test it.

    The imperial doctor did not dare to cut it off.

    The servants even had to walk three feet away even when passing by.

    Because everyone began to doubt one thing——

    Who is killing people in the Prime Minister's Mansion?

    In the main hall, the atmosphere was extremely low.

    The Prime Minister stayed up all night and his eyes were black and blue.

    He looked at his stepmother.

    "Did you do this?"

    The stepmother's expression did not change.

    "What do you think, Master?"

    A rhetorical question makes the air colder.

    Su Rou stood aside, her fingertips trembling.

    For the first time she realized—

    Things got out of hand.

    It’s not that the round was unsuccessful.

    It was the game that started to bite back.

    "Where is Su Wan?"

    The prime minister asked suddenly.

    The steward replied in a low voice:

    "Back to you, sir...in the west courtyard."

    "She never came out."

    The prime minister frowned.

    "Call her."

    No one moved.

    Because no one dares.

    After yesterday’s game, everyone knew one thing——

    Su Wan is no longer "someone who can be called upon anytime".

    She is "the one who will turn the tables".

    In the end, Su Wan came by herself.

    When she walked into the main hall, everyone subconsciously fell silent for a moment.

    Not because of majesty.

    It’s because of the “unknown”.

    She was so calm.

    As calm as the storm last night had nothing to do with her.

    She stood in the center.

    "Looking for me?"

    The prime minister stared at her.

    "What do you think about Chun Xing's matter?"

    Su Wan glanced at him.

    "What are you asking about?"

    The prime minister was stunned.

    "What do you mean?"

    Su Wan whispered:

    "How did she die?"

    "That's why you want her to die."

    The air suddenly became tight.

    The stepmother's eyes darkened slightly.

    Su Rou subconsciously took half a step back.

    The prime minister's face looked ugly.

    "Are you blaming the prime minister?"

    Su Wan shook her head.

    "Not an accusation."

    "It's a summary."

    One sentence.

    Make the atmosphere even colder.

    The imperial doctor stood aside, his palms all sweaty.

    He didn't dare to look at Su Wan anymore.

    Because every word she said was too "accurate".

    Too accurate to be a guess.

    Like "see".

    The stepmother finally spoke.

    "Su Wan."

    "You said Chun Xing's death had nothing to do with the Prime Minister's Mansion."

    "Then please explain."
title_en: Chapter 9 She begins to doubt the cause of her mother’s death
